title: DataAccessV1dot12
description: K-05 v1.12, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1248, from the D-017 path audit's line 26 'F2' and ruling R5; QUESTIONS.md CQ-206 and CQ-214; DL-498). It only adds to v1.11 (data-access.v1.11.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to v1.10 and through it to every earlier version down to v1): every v1.11 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes, so every v1 to v1.11 exchange is a v1.12 exchange. Added: five reads on the runtime side, the three behind staging's test-phone page (actions/src/page-calls/staging/test-phone/types.ts TesterAccess, TestPhoneRoster, PhoneStates) and the two behind the handle actor's copies (runtime/src/actor/copies/types.ts SafetyTimerSource, StoppedFlagSource): readTesterStanding (README item 53: a session token's sha256 and a time give tester, notTester or noSession, from K-22 v1's session_for_token and K-36 v1's live team rows, never the session, the person or a hash), readRosterPhone (item 54: a roster phone's number and email on file, by the K-04 handle id the roster's list names), readPhoneState (item 55: a number's K-04 phone row as the page shows it, and its newest K-29 chat link's code and ready text), readLiveTimers (item 56: a handle's running and missed K-34 safety timers, the address sealed as stored) and readStoppedFlag (item 57: a handle's K-04 stopped flag and version, fresh). Each runs as rosie_job with no business scope, reads the primary uncached, writes nothing and reads K-04 v1, K-22 v1, K-29 v1, K-34 v1 and K-36 v1 as migrated (0004, 0012, 0013, 0016, 0017, 0020) with the grants rosie_job holds, so no column, grant, index, table or migration is added. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

tokenSha256.title: TokenSha256
tokenSha256.description: A session token's sha256 in lower-case hex, the form K-22 v1 sessions.token_sha256 stores (sessions_token_hash_form). The token is a key: the page entry hashes the cookie's token and sends this alone, so the token never reaches the database, a request, an answer, an error, a log or a span (K-21 v1 'Never in a span or a log'; README item 53). New in v1.12.

readTesterStanding.request.title: ReadTesterStandingRequest
readTesterStanding.request.description: The standing of the session a staging page call carries, for staging's test tools (README item 53; actions/src/page-calls/staging/test-phone/types.ts TesterAccess.standing; K-21 v1 README 'Staging only': 'a signed-in roster tester or a person on Rosie's team'). The page entry sends it after a request with a session token, before the roster or the phone is read (handlers.ts step 3). The request carries the token's sha256 and the time, never the token (refuse-tester-standing-token-not-hash) and never a person. Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope (K-22 v1 sessions and K-36 v1 team_page_recipients are scoped none; team_page_recipients grants rosie_app nothing: 0017; the team console's reads run on the runtime side: K-21 v1 'The team console'). Reads the primary, uncached: a session that ended or a team row removed ends the standing at once. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources; once per staging test-tool call. New in v1.12.

tokenSha256.description: The sha256 of the session token the page sent (K-21 v1 signedInPage.sessionToken), never the token itself.

at.description: The moment the session must be live at: the page entry's own clock (handlers.ts: utcSeconds(now)), K-22 v1 session_for_token's at.

readTesterStanding.response.title: ReadTesterStandingResponse
readTesterStanding.response.description: The standing alone (README item 53, defaults 103 and 104): never the session, the person, a hash or whether a person or a team row exists, so a call that is no tester's learns only notTester, and a call with no live session only noSession (K-21 v1 notTester, signInNeeded; refuse-tester-standing-names-person). New in v1.12.

standing.description: tester: a live session (K-22 v1 session_for_token answers a row) whose person holds a live K-36 v1 team_page_recipients row, removed_at null (README default 103); notTester: a live session whose person holds none; noSession: no live session has the hash at the time, whether the hash is unknown, the session ended (signed out, contact changed, left, handed over) or it expired (README default 104).

readTesterStanding.errors.title: ReadTesterStandingErrors
readTesterStanding.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again; the page entry answers 503 meanwhile, and no tool is used on a standing not read. A read writes nothing. New in v1.12.

readTesterStanding.exchange.title: ReadTesterStandingExchange
readTesterStanding.exchange.description: One readTesterStanding request with its outcome: the standing, or transient. New in v1.12.

emailOnFile.title: EmailOnFile
emailOnFile.description: An email address as K-04 v1 handles stores one of kind email (handles_address_form: one @, no space, lower case). New in v1.12.

rosterPhone.title: RosterPhone
rosterPhone.description: A roster test phone as the page's roster gives it (actions/src/page-calls/staging/test-phone/types.ts RosterPhone, less its roster id, which the binding holds): its number and the email on file for its one person (README item 54, default 107). Never the person, a name or another handle. New in v1.12.

number.description: K-04 handles.address of the phone handle: its number in E.164 form (handles_address_form), the number the seed wrote and the page sends as. Never logged or put in a span; the page shows its last four digits alone.

email.description: The email on file: when the phone handle has exactly one person (K-04 person_handles), the address of that person's one K-04 handle of kind email; null when the handle has none or several people, or the person none or several email handles (README default 107), so the page lists no email.

readRosterPhone.request.title: ReadRosterPhoneRequest
readRosterPhone.request.description: A roster test phone's number and email on file (README item 54; actions/src/page-calls/staging/test-phone/types.ts TestPhoneRoster.phone). The roster's list, which roster id is which K-04 handle, is staging's config, kept as the seed's own (README default 106; K-21 v1 default 6), so the binding finds the roster id's handle id there and sends it: the request names that handle alone, never a roster id (refuse-roster-phone-by-roster-id) or a number. Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope (K-04 handles and person_handles are tables only rosie_job reads: 0012). Reads the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources; once per staging test-phone call, after the tester's standing. New in v1.12.

handleId.description: K-04 handles.id the roster's list gives for the roster id (tp-01: handle-sam, T-1148's TEST_OWNER_1; tp-02 to tp-05: handle-<roster id>, T-202's db/seeds/staging-core.ts).

readRosterPhone.response.title: ReadRosterPhoneResponse
readRosterPhone.response.description: The roster phone, or none when K-04 holds no phone handle by that id: no handle (the seed has not written it) or one of kind email (README default 107). None is an answer, not an error, as for v1.10's handle reads (README default 95): the binding answers the page's roster null, so the call answers notTestPhone and nothing is signed or posted. New in v1.12.

handleId.description: The request's handle id (K-08 v1 handleRef).

phone.description: The phone's number and email on file, or null for no phone handle by that id.

readRosterPhone.errors.title: ReadRosterPhoneErrors
readRosterPhone.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again; the page entry answers 503 meanwhile. A read writes nothing. New in v1.12.

readRosterPhone.exchange.title: ReadRosterPhoneExchange
readRosterPhone.exchange.description: One readRosterPhone request with its outcome: the roster phone, none, or transient. New in v1.12.

phoneStateOpen.title: PhoneStateOpen
phoneStateOpen.description: A phone row that is not stopped (K-04 v1 phones.stopped false): its chat open or closed, and no STOP in force, even when stop_at keeps the last STOP's time after a START (DL-193; README default 108). New in v1.12.

stoppedAt.description: No STOP is in force, so none: never stop_at after a START (refuse-phone-state-stopped-at-after-start).

phoneStateStopped.title: PhoneStateStopped
phoneStateStopped.description: A stopped phone row (K-04 v1 phones.stopped true): Rosie's texts to it are off for every business until START (MC C1; RULES 7.2), its chat closed (phones_stop_closes_chat), and the STOP in force came at stop_at (phones_stopped_has_time). New in v1.12.

chatOpen.description: K-04 v1 phones.chat_open: false for a stopped phone (phones_stop_closes_chat).

stoppedAt.description: K-04 v1 phones.stop_at: when the STOP in force came (actions/src/page-calls/staging/test-phone/types.ts PhoneState.stoppedAt).

chatLinkRead.title: ChatLinkRead
chatLinkRead.description: A phone's chat link as K-29 v1 chat_links stores it: its short code and its ready text, which holds the code (chat_links_ready_text_has_code). The link's address is not stored: the binding builds it in K-09 v1 issueChatLink's form from Rosie's number, a config value (README default 109; Q-51). Never the link's id, person, business, booking or purpose. New in v1.12.

readyText.description: K-29 v1 chat_links.ready_text, word for word: the text the phone sends to open its chat (MC C9; RULES 4.1b). Never logged or put in a span.

readPhoneState.request.title: ReadPhoneStateRequest
readPhoneState.request.description: A roster phone's own state as staging's test-phone page shows it (README item 55; actions/src/page-calls/staging/test-phone/types.ts PhoneStates.state; K-21 v1 testPhoneParts: 'the stop state; the chat link with its ready text'). The request names the number (K-04 phones.number, the row's key), which the binding has from readRosterPhone. Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope (K-04 phones is a table only rosie_job reads: 0012; a test phone's chat links may be any business's, K-29 chat_links behind rosie_job's runtime policy). Reads the primary, uncached (K-21 v1 README 'Who may call': every call). Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources; once per testPhoneParts call. New in v1.12.

number.description: The roster phone's number in E.164 form. Never logged or put in a span.

readPhoneState.noRow.title: ReadPhoneStateNoRow
readPhoneState.noRow.description: K-04 holds no phone row for the number: its first text has not come (K-05 v1.7 openChatOnText writes the row at receipt). No chat link can name it (chat_links_phone_fk). The binding answers chat closed and not stopped (PhoneState.chatOpen: 'false while the phone has no row yet'; README default 108). New in v1.12.

chatLink.description: None: a number with no phone row has no chat link (refuse-phone-state-link-without-phone).

readPhoneState.row.title: ReadPhoneStateRow
readPhoneState.row.description: The number's phone row and its newest chat link (README item 55). New in v1.12.

phone.description: The row's chat open, stopped and the STOP in force (README default 108).

chatLink.description: The phone's newest K-29 chat link by issued_at, a tie to the lower id, whatever its purpose, business or use; null when it has none (README default 109).

readPhoneState.response.title: ReadPhoneStateResponse
readPhoneState.response.description: The number's state, or no row. It names no number (refuse-phone-state-answers-number): the request holds it. New in v1.12.

readPhoneState.errors.title: ReadPhoneStateErrors
readPhoneState.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again; the page entry answers 503 meanwhile. A read writes nothing. New in v1.12.

readPhoneState.exchange.title: ReadPhoneStateExchange
readPhoneState.exchange.description: One readPhoneState request with its outcome: the state, no row, or transient. New in v1.12.

sealedBytes.title: SealedBytes
sealedBytes.description: A sealed column's bytes as PostgreSQL stores them (bytea), written in its hex text form: a backslash, x, and two lower-case hex digits a byte, as K-34 v1's seed-safety-timer.json writes safety_timers.address. The bytes are sealed under one person's key (K-34 rule 6; db/repo/sealing.ts): never opened, decoded or put in plain words on the way (refuse-live-timers-address-opened). New in v1.12.

liveTimer.title: LiveTimer
liveTimer.description: One live K-34 v1 safety_timers row of the handle, the thirteen columns the actor's copy keeps (runtime/src/actor/copies/types.ts SafetyTimerRow; arch 11 line 566: 'the actor's copy of its due time, address and emergency contact'), each named here in K-05's form for its K-34 column (README item 56). Never the timer's other columns. New in v1.12.

businessId.description: K-34 safety_timers.business_id: the business of the job the timer covers, any business (no business scope).

workerHandleId.description: K-34 safety_timers.worker_handle_id: the pro's handle, the request's.

emergencyContactPersonId.description: K-34 safety_timers.emergency_contact_person_id: the contact who said yes.

emergencyContactHandleId.description: K-34 safety_timers.emergency_contact_handle_id: the contact's handle, which the copy reaches while PostgreSQL is down.

dueAt.description: K-34 safety_timers.due_at: the check-out time, in UTC.

dueZone.description: K-34 safety_timers.due_zone: the IANA zone it was given in (safety_timers_due_zone_form).

address.description: K-34 safety_timers.address: the job's address, sealed under address_for_person_id's key, as stored (README default 110).

addressForPersonId.description: K-34 safety_timers.address_for_person_id: the person whose key seals the address.

clockRowId.description: K-34 safety_timers.clock_row_id: the core clock row that fires the miss while PostgreSQL is up.

state.description: K-34 safety_timers.state: running, or missed (a missed check stays open until SAFE: S13-10). A safe timer is never live, so never answered (refuse-live-timers-safe-listed).

version.description: K-34 safety_timers.version: the copy is the row at this version.

readLiveTimers.request.title: ReadLiveTimersRequest
readLiveTimers.request.description: The reload of a handle's live safety timers for its actor's copy (README item 56; runtime/src/actor/copies/types.ts SafetyTimerSource.liveTimers; K-34 v1 safety_timers_worker_live_idx: 'the actor reloads its copies'). The actor sends it after a commit that may have written a timer row, and after a commit whose answer was lost (copies.ts refreshTimers). The request names the handle alone, never a business (refuse-live-timers-business-scope): a read under one business's scope would hide another business's timers and empty the copy of a live one (README default 110). Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope (K-34 safety_timers behind rosie_job's runtime policy: 0016). Reads the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources. New in v1.12.

handleId.description: K-04 handles.id of the actor's handle (K-34 safety_timers.worker_handle_id).

readLiveTimers.response.title: ReadLiveTimersResponse
readLiveTimers.response.description: The handle's live timers: K-34 safety_timers whose worker_handle_id is the handle and whose state is running or missed, at every business, earliest due_at first, a tie to the lower id; none is an empty list, an answer (README item 56, default 110). New in v1.12.

handleId.description: The request's handle id (K-08 v1 handleRef).

readLiveTimers.errors.title: ReadLiveTimersErrors
readLiveTimers.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again; the copy keeps what it holds and stays marked stale, so a later commit reloads (copies.ts reloadTimers). A read writes nothing. New in v1.12.

readLiveTimers.exchange.title: ReadLiveTimersExchange
readLiveTimers.exchange.description: One readLiveTimers request with its outcome: the live timers, or transient. New in v1.12.

readStoppedFlag.request.title: ReadStoppedFlagRequest
readStoppedFlag.request.description: The re-read of a handle's stopped flag for its actor's copy, after a commit whose answer was lost (README item 57; runtime/src/actor/copies/types.ts StoppedFlagSource.stoppedFlag; T-1206; DL-427). The request names the actor's handle alone, never a number (refuse-stopped-flag-by-number). Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope (K-04 phones is a table only rosie_job reads: 0012). Reads the primary, never a replica or a cache, in its own transaction begun after the call is sent: a read the copy takes ends the lost commits' marks noted before it was sent, so a stale read could end a mark on a flag it never saw (T-1206's security note a; README default 111). Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources. New in v1.12.

handleId.description: K-04 handles.id of the actor's handle (K-04 phones.handle_id, phones_handle_key).

readStoppedFlag.response.title: ReadStoppedFlagResponse
readStoppedFlag.response.description: The handle's K-04 phones row's stopped flag and version (README item 57): the flag is one for every business (MC C1), and the version orders the copy's writes (copies.ts takeStopped). New in v1.12.

handleId.description: The request's handle id (K-08 v1 handleRef).

phoneVersion.description: K-04 v1 phones.version (K-09 v1 recordStopOrStart's phoneVersion): never left out (refuse-stopped-flag-no-version).

phoneNotFoundError.title: PhoneNotFoundError
phoneNotFoundError.description: K-04 holds no phone row for the handle: an email handle, or a phone whose first text has not come. The port has no answer for none (StoppedFlagAnswer), so the copy reads it as a failed re-read and keeps the stricter reading, a lost commit's mark included; it is never answered as not stopped (README default 111). Nothing was written. New in v1.12.

rowId.description: The request's handle id, which the row was looked up by (phones_handle_key).

readStoppedFlag.errors.title: ReadStoppedFlagErrors
readStoppedFlag.errors.description: notFound (table phones): no phone row for the handle; transient: the same request may be sent again. Each leaves the copy as it was, the stricter reading included (copies.ts readStoppedAgain). A read writes nothing. New in v1.12.

readStoppedFlag.exchange.title: ReadStoppedFlagExchange
readStoppedFlag.exchange.description: One readStoppedFlag request with its outcome: the flag and its version, or one of its errors. New in v1.12.
